daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR has passed the Asset Forfeiture Bill into law after 18 years of deliberation, with House Speaker Puan Maharani stating the law was not approved due to pressure. The legislation, which the head of Commission III credits to initiator Dasco, aims to facilitate the seizure of illegally obtained assets, though the latest draft remains inaccessible to the public.

  • The National Police are holding a case review on alleged treason against President Prabowo, involving Propam and the National Police Commission after obtaining new evidence in the case.
  • The KPK has questioned the Director General of ATR/BPN regarding mechanisms for issuing land use rights certificates.
  • Grace Natalie confirmed that PSI supports the Prabowo government despite having no members in the cabinet.
  • Subhan Palal has denied political party affiliation behind the lawsuit challenging Vice President Gibran's academic credentials.
  • The KPK is investigating alleged illicit payments to BPK in connection with the Pemalang regent case.
  • Pukat UGM has noted that the KPK is not mentioned in the Asset Forfeiture Bill.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, where he and Russian President Putin discussed bilateral issues following the APEC dinner. Indonesia and China have agreed on strategic cooperation valued at Rp1,300 trillion.

  • The Defence Minister has inspected construction of new facilities at Haluoleo Air Force Base.
  • Indonesia and South Korea are expanding marine workforce training cooperation.
  • CTARSA, YRKB, and the Indonesian Fleet Command have sent 5 tons of aid to forest fire survivors in Kalimantan.
  • Senator Dino highlighted threats and intimidation against freedom of expression.

Other

The Ministry of Manpower announced that minimum wage determination will balance living needs with economic conditions. Bank Indonesia has assured that its recent rate hike will not derail economic growth, while the rupiah is predicted to weaken to between Rp18,180-18,300 per US dollar.

  • The Ministry of Health has explained the issue of viral "dental immunization" that risks cross-contamination.
  • Taiwan detained Indonesian pepper product Ladaku after finding two pesticide residues in the ground pepper.
  • The government stated that Javan rhinos will not be relocated without comprehensive assessment.
  • Jambi authorities have released five rehabilitated orangutans into the wild.
  • Authorities have closed 31 illegal gold mines in Gunung Talaga, Bogor.
  • The Ministry of Religion is preparing civil service teacher positions for 2027, allowing contract teachers to apply.
